_readme: Every credit for Cassini OS, in one place: build.py bakes this file into the About window (about.html). Add an entry to the group it belongs to whenever a page starts using new data, a new map, a model, a sound, a library or a font. Fields: id (short, unique; a callout elsewhere on the page links to it with data-about="<id>"), title, credit (the attribution line, as the source asks for it), short (optional: the few words a callout on the page shows), detail (optional: what it is and how Cassini OS uses it), license, url (optional), files (optional: the files under web/replay/data/textures it covers, without the 1k/2k/4k folder; build.py refuses to build while a file there has no entry), note (optional: anything still to do, such as a missing license).

entries.title: Cassini camera pictures
entries.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Space Science Institute
entries.detail: Every picture in the camera windows, mosaics, color sets, movies and highlights is a frame from Cassini's Imaging Science Subsystem (the narrow-angle and wide-angle cameras), archived by NASA's Planetary Data System, Cartography and Imaging Sciences Node. Cassini OS calibrates, stacks, aligns and centers them with SPICE; the colors are its own reconstruction, not NASA's.
entries.license: NASA material, not copyrighted in the US (NASA media usage guidelines)

entries.title: Trajectory, pointing and planet positions
entries.credit: NASA/JPL Navigation and Ancillary Information Facility (NAIF), Cassini SPICE archive co-s_j_e_v-spice-6-v1.0
entries.detail: Where Cassini, the planets and the moons were, which way Cassini pointed (its reconstructed attitude kernels), and the camera frames. Read with SpiceyPy.
entries.license: NASA material, not copyrighted in the US

entries.title: Camera calibration
entries.credit: Cassini ISS team: CISSCAL and the Cassini ISS Data User's Guide (Porco et al. 2004; West et al. 2010; Knowles et al. 2020)
entries.detail: The steps and constants Cassini OS uses to turn raw frames into brightness (I/F): the bias, exposure, gain and per-filter sensitivity, and each filter's effective wavelength.
entries.license: Published by NASA's Planetary Data System

entries.title: Grand Finale readings
entries.credit: NASA Planetary Data System, Planetary Plasma Interactions Node; Cassini INMS (Southwest Research Institute), MAG (Imperial College London) and RPWS (University of Iowa) teams
entries.detail: The real readings from Cassini's last hour shown in the Grand Finale: INMS raw count rates (counts, not densities), the magnetometer at full resolution, and RPWS 60 s key parameters, from 15 September 2017.
entries.license: NASA material, not copyrighted in the US

entries.title: Mission facts and numbers
entries.credit: NASA, NASA/JPL and ESA mission pages
entries.detail: The facts on the loading screen (each one names its source as it shows), and the numbers and timings the Grand Finale is pinned to (JPL, "Cassini Spacecraft Makes Its Final Approach to Saturn", 13 September 2017; "Cassini by the Numbers"), and the opening at the start of the mission (ESA, "Cassini-Huygens: Launch information"; NASA, "Cassini Quick Facts").

entries.title: Huygens descent pictures
entries.credit: ESA/NASA/JPL/University of Arizona; mosaics by Erich Karkoschka (DISR team)
entries.detail: The probe's own pictures of Titan from its Descent Imager/Spectral Radiometer (DISR), and the nested mosaics of the landing site (60 m down to 1 m per pixel) Erich Karkoschka assembled from them, from ESA's Planetary Science Archive (HP-SSA-DISR-2-3-EDR-RDR-V1.3).

entries.title: Huygens trajectory
entries.credit: ESA Huygens Descent Trajectory Working Group (B. Kazeminejad, ESTEC), HP-SSA-DTWG-6-TRAJECTORY-V2.0; NASA/JPL NAIF
entries.detail: The probe's path through Titan's atmosphere to the ground; its coast from Cassini to Titan comes from NAIF's reconstructed trajectory.

groups.title: Surface maps and shapes
groups.note: Maps come from the Celestia project's CelestiaContent collection, resized into the 1k, 2k and 4k sizes; credit lines follow Celestia's license files. Maps marked "No license stated" are reworks of NASA/JPL and other material without a license file and will be rebuilt from public-domain originals before a public launch.

entries.title: Sonification
entries.credit: Made for Cassini OS, after Erich Karkoschka's "Titan Descent Data Movie with Bells and Whistles" (DISR team, University of Arizona)
entries.detail: The default sounds are synthesized in the browser from what Cassini is doing; the idea of a chime for each instrument part follows Karkoschka's Huygens descent movie.

entries.title: Instrument notes
entries.credit: Instrument samples: Versilian Community Sample Library and VSCO 2 Community Edition, Versilian Studios (CC0)
entries.detail: The recorded notes that Settings > Sound > Instrument can play instead of the synthesized chimes: Steinway B grand piano, hand chimes, glockenspiel, vibraphone (soft mallets and bowed), marimba, Tanzanian kalimba, concert harp, tubular bells, rubbed wine glasses, quiet pipe organ and Nepalese hand bells from VCSL; the violin and cello sections from VSCO 2 CE. One recording per note, trimmed and pitched to the scale (web/cassini-os/sounds/make_sounds.py).
